Why This Is Asked

Tests practical design of a per-tenant feature flag system in a CNF gateway stack, focusing on CRD design, a lean central policy API, and a sidecar with token authentication and caching.

Key Concepts

- Kubernetes CRD for per-tenant feature flags
- Sidecar fetch with short lived token and 60s cache
- Default semantics and tenant isolation
- End-to-end test in a single namespace

Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal CRD example
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: featureflags.cnf.example.com
spec:
  group: cnf.example.com
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              perTenantFlags:
                type: object
              defaultEnabled:
                type: boolean
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: featureflags
    singular: featureflag
    kind: FeatureFlag
    shortNames:
    - ff
```

- How would you handle policy changes during traffic and cache invalidation?
- How would you audit tenant flag usage and prevent leakage across tenants?

## Why This Is Asked
This tests ability to implement zero-downtime upgrades in a multi-tenant CNF gateway, focusing on per-tenant isolation, cross-namespace coordination, and robust failure handling.

## Key Concepts
- Graceful drain: per-tenant drain window, preStop, readiness gates
- Global upgrade control: ConfigMap flag
- Control-plane signaling: endpoint or event
- Failure modes: stuck drains, failed signal, burst load

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-upgrade
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  upgradePause: "true"
```

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway-tenant-a
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: gateway
          image: cnf/gateway:latest
          lifecycle:
            preStop:
              exec:
                command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:9000/drain || true"]
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 9000
              protocol: HTTP
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 5
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the drain behavior under bursty traffic?
- How would you handle tenants with long-lived streams (WebSockets)?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical skills in implementing controlled, observable deployments in a multi-tenant CNF gateway environment. It checks familiarity with canary strategies, per-tenant isolation, and metric-driven promotion/rollback.

## Key Concepts

- Canary deployments with Argo Rollouts
- Per-tenant traffic shaping and isolation
- Prometheus-based SLIs and analysis templates
- Automated rollback and promotion thresholds
- End-to-end testing in a single-tenant namespace before broader rollout

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: gateway-rollout-tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
      tenant: a
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
        tenant: a
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: registry.example.com/cnf/gateway:latest
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
      - setWeight: 10
      - pause: { duration: 5m }
      - setWeight: 100
      analysis:
        templates:
        - templateName: canary-metrics
        metrics:
        - name: latency
          interval: 30s
          successCondition: result < 0.001 * 0.15
        - name: error-rate
          interval: 30s
          successCondition: result < 0.005
```

```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AnalysisTemplate
metadata:
  name: canary-metrics
spec:
  metrics:
  - name: latency
    provider:
      prometheus:
        url: http://prometheus.k8s.svc
        query: sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_sum[5m])) / sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count[5m]))
  - name: error-rate
    provider:
      prometheus:
        url: http://prometheus.k8s.svc
        query: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status!~"2.."}[5m]))
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you adapt this for cross-cluster canaries?
- What monitoring dashboards would you expose to operators for this flow?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to architect cross-cluster, tenant-isolated config rollouts with dynamic proxy configuration.

## Key Concepts
- Envoy xDS dynamic configuration and Aggregated Discovery Service (ADS)
- Kubernetes CRD-based policy model per tenant with isolation
- Canary traffic shaping with weight and time-based rollout window
- Multi-cluster consistency and safe rollback mechanisms
- Observability hooks for validation during rollout phases

## Code Example
```yaml
# (a) Tenant Routing Policy with Canary Weight and Rollout Window
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: TenantRoutePolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-api-v2
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  tenant: tenant-a
  targetCluster: cluster-west
  route:
    path: /api/v2
    backendRefs:
      - name: gateway-service
        port: 8080
  canary:
    weight: 0  # Start at 0%
    rolloutDuration: 30m
    stepWeight: 10  # Increment by 10% each step
    stepInterval: 5m
  rollback:
    enabled: true
    failureThreshold: 5  # Rollback if 5 consecutive errors exceed threshold
    errorRateThreshold: 0.05  # 5% error rate triggers rollback
  healthCheck:
    endpoint: /healthz
    interval: 30s
    timeout: 10s
---
# (b) Sidecar Config to Watch Policy and Push Updates
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: envoy-gateway-sidecar
  namespace: gateway-system
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: xds-controller
          image: cnf/xds-controller:latest
          args:
            - --policy-namespace=tenant-a
            - --xds-address=$(POD_IP):18000
            - --sync-interval=10s
          env:
            - name: POD_IP
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef:
                  fieldPath: status.podIP
          volumeMounts:
            - name: policy-config
              mountPath: /etc/policy
              readOnly: true
        - name: envoy
          image: envoyproxy/envoy:latest
          args:
            - --config-path /etc/envoy/envoy.yaml
            - --service-cluster gateway
          volumeMounts:
            - name: envoy-config
              mountPath: /etc/envoy
      volumes:
        - name: policy-config
          configMap:
            name: tenant-policies
        - name: envoy-config
          emptyDir: {}
---
# (c) One-Namespace Test Manifest for Canary Rollout and Rollback
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: CanaryRolloutTest
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-canary-test
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  policyRef:
    name: tenant-a-api-v2
  testStages:
    - stage: baseline
      duration: 5m
      expectedWeight: 0
      checks:
        - type: metrics
          metric: requests_total{path="/api/v2"}
          condition: equals 0
    - stage: canary_10pct
      duration: 10m
      expectedWeight: 10
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/health
          expectSuccessRate: 0.95
        - type: metrics
          metric: envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_xx{cluster="backend-v2"}
          condition: exists
    - stage: canary_50pct
      duration: 10m
      expectedWeight: 50
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/api/v2/users
          expectSuccessRate: 0.99
    - stage: full_rollout
      duration: 5m
      expectedWeight: 100
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/api/v2/**
          expectSuccessRate: 0.999
  rollbackTest:
    enabled: true
    triggerFailureAt: canary_50pct
    expectedBehavior: weight_reverts_to_0_within_2m
```
